find: at.set(x - dx * back, BULLET_Y, y - dy * back);
replace: at.set(x + dx * back, BULLET_Y, y + dy * back);
why: Lays the dashes out AHEAD of the shell instead of behind it. The count would still be right, but a row in front of a shell reads as its direction of travel -- the trajectory preview issue #688 rules out -- and it covers exactly the ground the player is trying to read.
killedBy: shell bounce-trail system (issue #688) lays the row out behind the shell along its heading, at shell height
shell bounce-trail system (issue #688) turns the row with the shell the frame its heading turns
shell bounce-trail system (issue #688) follows the interpolated shell, not the tick position
